does: Stirs a food that is already cooked into a hot sauce and leaves it only until it is hot, so that it stays moist and whole instead of cooking further.

intro.what: An already cooked food is stirred into a hot sauce just long enough to heat it.
intro.why: Canned fish and cooked meats are ready to eat. More cooking only dries them or breaks them up.

how: Have the sauce hot and ready.
Add the cooked food in large pieces and fold it in gently.
Leave it only until it is hot, then go on at once.

cues.text: The pieces are hot and moist and still hold their shape.
A piece pressed with a spoon is warm through and still tender.

mistakes.mistake: Simmering the food in the sauce for a long time, so that it turns dry and stringy.
mistakes.fix: Add it at the end and leave it only until hot.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring hard, so that it breaks into shreds.
mistakes.fix: Fold it in gently in large pieces.

quiz.question: Why is canned tuna only warmed in the sauce?
choices: It is already cooked, and more cooking dries it.
It needs a long time to cook.
quiz.because: Cooked food only needs heat, not more cooking.

quiz.question: When does the cooked food go in?
choices: At the end, into the hot sauce.
quiz.because: Going in at the end keeps it moist.

quiz.question: How should the pieces look when ready?
choices: Hot, moist and still in pieces.
quiz.because: They should be heated but not broken down.

quiz.question: The tuna turned dry and stringy. What would you change next time?
choices: Add it at the end and heat it only briefly.

variant_of.differs: The food is not brought back to the boil on its own: it is only heated in a sauce that is already hot, for as short a time as possible.
